turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. My son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first; I want to know who decided that, and on what basis.
Okay. Let's look at the essay.
Before the essay, you skipped my question. Your own procedure, 4.2, says you call the parent before any mark is entered, and you didn't; who decided to enter that zero first?
You're very sharp, you know that?
Don't manage me, Hale. Who entered the zero, and when?
No, really. You caught the timestamp issue in thirty seconds. That's sharp.
"Timestamp issue." It's not a timestamp issue, it's my son learning about a zero on his phone in front of his class, and I'm still waiting for a name.
I just keep thinking, someone that sharp must see why I had to flag it.
"Had to." Then show me why, because so far I've heard compliments and no documents.
